concept.reason: Actual same-species anatomy and explicit conservative composite inference suffice. No generated concept or extra comparison art required.

scope: Complete living reconstruction of Pachycormus macropterus using explicitly combined same-species BRLSI anatomical evidence. Not a single specimen digital twin. Preserve whole fish, compact fusiform body and long scythe-like pectoral fins; no slab or exposed fossil skeleton.

scientific_limits.en: Head, forebody, pectoral and caudal evidence comes from different same-species specimens, not a complete single skeleton. Body subdivisions, body width, fleshed contour, fin spread and repaired caudal tips are inferred. The selected0.65m total length is a representative reconstruction estimate within published23.5–85cm total-length range, not a measurement of an assembled specimen. BRLSI M1393 tail distal rays are broken at the nodule margin; its exact living edge is unknown. Caudal anatomy varies among referred material and taxonomic significance remains unresolved. Do not copy taphonomic distortion, cracks or plaster as living features. Color is artistic. The unavailable Cooper2023 whole-body image was not viewed or used as a visual anchor.
scientific_limits.zh: 头、前躯、胸鳍和尾部来自多个同种标本，并非单个完整骨架。躯干分段比例、体宽、软组织轮廓、鳍展开和尾端补全均推定。选定0.65米全长是在论文23.5–85厘米全长范围内的代表复原估值，不是组合标本实测。BRLSI M1393尾鳍末端被结核边界截断，准确活体边缘不明；不同归属材料尾骨差异的分类意义未定。不得把埋藏变形、裂隙或石膏当活体特征。颜色艺术推定。未取得的Cooper2023全体图未查看、未作视觉锚。

specimen_lock.primary_anatomical_series: BRLSI Strawberry Bank specimens described by Cawley et al.2018/2019
specimen_lock.head: BRLSI M1332 lateral and M1389 dorsal
specimen_lock.pectoral: BRLSI M1395 complete pectoral, Fig5; M1332 also described with complete pectoral
specimen_lock.dorsal_anal: M1366 dorsal/M1341 anal described in same paper; anal fragmented
specimen_lock.interval: Early Jurassic, lower Toarcian, marine Strawberry Bank, UK

scale.basis: Cawley et al. specimen-series range. Selected0.65m is estimated representative total, not standard length or exact size of any chosen component specimen.
scale.precision_limit: Component numbers are approximate artist reconstruction targets, not measured fossil dimensions. Preserve natural scythe outline; do not elongate into unsupported sword or flying-fish wing merely to satisfy word long.

morphology: Compact fusiform fish body, deepest around shoulder/anterior trunk and tapering to narrow caudal peduncle. Not eel-like and not deep disc-shaped. Large head integrates into body with a short tapered snout.

Pair of substantial scythe-like pectoral fins attached low behind opercular region, gently swept backward with curved leading outline and concave trailing portion toward pointed tip. Actual complete M1395 fin is visible in Fig5; do not substitute a triangular shark flipper, straight paddle or huge wing.
Small dorsal fin on posterior half of trunk, anterior to the anal fin. Small anal near the tail. No pelvic fins, consistent with published genus diagnosis. No adipose fin or added dorsal finlets.

Deeply forked vertically oriented caudal fin, using published same-species morphology and M1393 rays; distal tips and precise edge reconstructed conservatively. Do not extrapolate giant sickle tail lobes from another pachycormid.

Short rostrum, sizable eye and gently domed posterior skull roof; maintain opercular transition. Small needle-like teeth may be simplified, no massive canine row. Near-closed mouth, neutral swimming pose.
Subtle rhombic scales may be suggested by facets; no protruding plate armor. Neutral grey/olive with lighter underside is artistic, not a taxonomic marker.

shape_gate.original_required_combination: Shape criterion: compact fusiform body and long sickle-shaped pectoral fins. Retain this anatomical combination when compared with nearby forms; a name, scale or pose change alone does not qualify.

original_requirements_audit.taxon_specific_evidence: Actual same-species complete pectoral and skull/forebody/tail evidence plus author fusiform diagnosis; composite explicitly disclosed.

shape_gate.comparison: Compare actual model pectoral outline against Cawley Fig5 and skull/forebody against Fig2/4, not merely this text. Against Aspidorhynchus-type slender unequal-jaw fish, compact body, short snout and substantial curved pectorals must remain different without color/name/scale. No external runtime model dependency.
acceptance: Lateral front: compact fusiform full body, short snout, dorsal anterior to anal and no pelvic fins.
Top: both scythe-like pectorals are separately legible beyond body with tapering curved tips and integrated roots; cannot be hidden against flank.
Head-on side: conservative reconstructed width and paired pectoral attachment, no paper-flat fossil slab.
Whole perspective: compact fusiform plus long scythe pectorals visibly coexist; label, palette or pose alone cannot establish gate.
